column1: # Sweep of the army enrolment drawer that holds Pablo Armando's card.
# FamilySearch image group #112342450 ("Fichas de enrolamiento", Ejercito Argentino), volume "Cajon 985 (Lera)".
# Method: the viewer's IMAGE INDEX panel is an HTML table, so each card's indexed content can be read as
# text without reading the handwriting. Only cards that LOOK like ours were then opened as images.
# Read 10 September 2026, images 650-688 (see the caution below).
# *** CAUTION ON THE IMAGE NUMBERS. *** The viewer's image-number box and the underlying image arks do
# NOT stay in step across loads: the same number returned a different ark on a second pass, and the
# indexed content ran one frame ahead of the box on part of the first pass. The numbers below are
# APPROXIMATE LOCATORS, good to about one frame - the same hazard already recorded for the Rosario film.
# What is fixed and citable: Pablo Armando's card is image ark 3:1:3QHK-MQL4-NQWN, and the LERENA
# section of the drawer opens with a tabbed guide card lettered "Lere. n." immediately before it.
# The people listed below were all actually read; only their frame numbers are soft.
# *** The drawer is NOT alphabetical by spelling. It is grouped by SOUND. *** Lera, Lerena, Lorena,
# Serena, Sera, Era, Leza, Perena, Perella and Hereijo are interfiled. That is why the index's "Lorena"
# and "Serena" manglings survived: the clerk who filed the cards was already treating them as one name.
